gridOwnsDayInstances.defectFoundAndFixed: the grid first held week INSTANCES carrying only a week number, so every week rendered week one seven days and week one states — the same seven days three times. It compiled and held its fixed point and was not a calendar.
gridOwnsDayInstances.whyAnInstanceCannotCarryIt: day state varies WITHIN a week (one today, one selected, leading days outside) while a component instance picks ONE variant for the whole component. Table gets away with row instances because a row is selected or not as a unit; a week is not.
gridOwnsDayInstances.resolution: the calendar grid owns day instances directly, each picking its own State variant and carrying its own Label. calendar/week-set stays as the published week template.
gridOwnsDayInstances.regressionTest: each week in the grid carries its OWN days and states

reviewedSource.todayRingCarriedNotDropped: astryx marks TODAY with an inset 1px ring and NO background, and SELECTED with a background and no ring. A background+text model would have lost the today marker entirely, so DayStateTokens gained an optional ring and calendar@1 emits it as an inside stroke.

receipts.what: the dark half of every astryx light-dark() colour pair
receipts.why: calendar@1 carries one colour mode; the dark half is a second Figma variable mode, not a missing colour

dateGrammarProblemSolved.problem: examples/day-picker/PROVENANCE.md records that the capture grammar cannot spell a Date, so a calendar driven by a live clock has a today ring and a visible month that move between captures and never byte-compare
dateGrammarProblemSolved.resolution: calendar@1 carries the month that was RENDERED as content (caption, weekdays, weeks of labelled day states), not a Date to re-render from. Determinism comes from the content being data. No $date marker was invented.
